fact: ITWeb Africa reports, citing Angola's telecommunications ministry (MINTTICS), that Angola and Mozambique signed a bilateral memorandum in June 2026 under which Mozambique's Tmcel and TVM would use Angola's ANGOSAT-2 satellite for telecom and broadcast signals, with a commercial agreement still to be formalised.

ITWeb Africa reports that Angola's National Space Programme Management Office signed a commercial pilot agreement with Telecom Namibia to validate satellite-driven backhaul; the article gives no signing date, so the document's published date is used.

Angola Telecom's executive director said Angola Telecom and Telecom Namibia signed a memorandum of understanding in Swakopmund in March 2026 for the SARSSy submarine cable, with five Angolan landing points and a link to Equiano, due in service in June 2027.

Angola Telecom's executive director said a terrestrial fibre link between Angola (Santa Clara) and Namibia (Ondjiva) already exists and the two operators already provide telecom services in both directions.

O Economico reports that Angola's telecommunications minister Mario Oliveira and Mozambique's minister Americo Muchanga signed a memorandum of understanding at the V National Communications Conference for a Nacala-Lobito submarine cable, still in the concession phase.
